approachQuestion.prompt:
Blank Faulty Rows and Columns

An integer matrix board records measurements. Modify it in place: every row and every column that contains a zero in the ORIGINAL board must become entirely zero. All other cells retain their original values. Zeros written during the operation must not trigger additional rows or columns.

Example 1: board=[[1,0,3],[4,5,6]] → [[0,0,0],[4,0,6]].
Example 2: board=[[1,2],[0,4]] → [[0,2],[0,0]].
Example 3: board=[[7,8]] → [[7,8]].

Constraints:
1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000; all rows have length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Every zero is significant; there is no spare marker value.
Modify the existing matrix and return nothing. Rows and their storage must remain the same.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000; all rows have length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Every zero is significant; there is no spare marker value.
Modify the existing matrix and return nothing. Rows and their storage must remain the same.

options.text: First remember whether the original first row or first column contains a zero. Scan interior cells; for each original zero set its row’s first cell and column’s first cell to zero. Clear interior cells according to those markers, then clear the first row and column according to the two saved flags.
options.feedback: Interior values stay unchanged while markers are collected, so marker writes cannot create false evidence. The two flags preserve the original meaning of the first row and column.

options.text: Scan the original board to fill separate Boolean arrays recording rows and columns containing a zero. Then scan again and clear cells belonging to any marked row or column.
options.feedback: This correctly separates original evidence from writes, but separate marker arrays are removable because the first row and column can hold the markers with two flags.

options.text: Scan every position. Whenever its current value is zero, immediately clear its entire row and column, then continue scanning the changed board.
options.feedback: A newly written zero can wrongly cascade. In [[1,0],[1,1]], clearing the original zero writes zero at (1,1). When the scan later reaches that new zero, it clears row 1, destroying the 1 at (1,0) that should remain.

options.text: Use the first row and column as markers, but save only whether board[0][0] originally equals zero. At the end clear both the first row and column exactly when that flag is true.
options.feedback: The first row and column can require different treatment. [[1,0],[2,3]] must clear the first row and second column but preserve board[1][0]=2; the corner alone does not capture this.

feedback.reason: Newly written zeros must not be mistaken for original evidence.
details: Save two separate flags for original zeros in the first row and column. Mark interior zero rows and columns on that border. Apply the markers to the interior, then use the original flags to finish the border.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Store Markers on the Matrix Border”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let r and c be the dimensions. Indexed integer reads/writes cost constant time. Include all scans of the first row, first column and interior, including one-row or one-column boards. The mutated board is input storage; there is no returned storage. Count flags, indices and call stack. No new arrays, recursion or hashing are used.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000; all rows have length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Every zero is significant; there is no spare marker value.
Modify the existing matrix and return nothing. Rows and their storage must remain the same.

options.text: O(r*c) time, O(r + c) auxiliary space.
O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space for all dimensions.

feedback.reason: A fixed number of matrix scans reuse the input border as markers.
details: A fixed number of scans visits the border and interior. For positive dimensions, r+c is bounded by 2*r*c, so total worst-case time is O(r*c), even for one-dimensional boards. Only two flags and fixed index state are allocated outside the matrix.
The option “O(r*c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The original matrix safely supplies all growing marker storage.
The option “O(r*c) time, O(r + c) auxiliary space.”: Separate Boolean arrays describe the partial alternative, not the fixed method.
The option “O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space for all dimensions.”: When both dimensions grow, visiting the interior exceeds a border-only bound.
The option “O((r*c)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Rows and columns are not repeatedly cleared for every encountered zero.
